Hi Samir,

Thanks again for the time today — really appreciated the context on FinPath's fraud-detection and customer support use cases. Quick recap from my side:

- Primary goals: reduce latency for real-time scoring, lower per-token inference cost for high-volume support workflows, and ensure auditability for regulated data.
- Current stack: in-house feature store + batch model scoring; looking to add low-latency LLM inference for reranking and contextual responses.
- Success metrics: 100ms p90 inference for short prompts, <20% token cost reduction vs. current hosted baseline, and SOC2 evidence for procurement.

Next steps: we'd like to schedule a 60-minute demo + technical deep dive where our solutions engineer can walk through runtime architecture and quantization options. Proposed times (all in ET):
- Thu 7/15, 11:00 - 12:00 ET
- Thu 7/15, 15:00 - 16:00 ET
- Fri 7/16, 10:00 - 11:00 ET

If none of those work, share your availability and we can adjust.

Also, you mentioned looping in security and procurement — looping in our internal security lead Neha (neha_kapoor@redwood.com) and our solutions engineer Dev (dev_patel@redwood.com) on the next thread so we can cover SOC2 / architecture details as part of the deep dive. Attaching our SOC2 overview and a sample SLA to help procurement get started.

Attachments: SOC2-overview.pdf, SLA-draft.docx

Thanks,

Thanks all — happy to take the technical portion. A couple quick asks so I can tailor the deep dive:

- Typical request size and average sequence length for the support reranker?
- Expected QPS (avg and peak) for the fraud scoring path?
- Any regulatory constraints on token retention or logs (PII/HIPAA/GDPR relevant fields)?

I'll bring a short slide with benchmarked p90 numbers across quantization profiles and an architecture PDF (attaching inference-arch.pdf). If you can send the request size/QPS now, I can customize the demo to show realistic batching and KV cache behavior.

All set — accepted the 11:00 - 12:00 ET slot.

Quick answers to Dev's questions:
- Support reranker: avg request length ~120 tokens, p95 ~420 tokens.
- Fraud scoring: steady-state 25 QPS, peak bursts up to 150 QPS during batch windows.
- Data retention: we cannot persist raw PII in logs; derived metadata is OK. We'll have procurement/security bring any specific legal language.

See you Thursday — looking forward to the technical deep dive.

Samir
